key_insight: Iterative strong coupling stabilizes FD-SPH simulations of lightweight floating bodies where single-pass coupling fails, even with much smaller time steps.
engineering_relevance: The method supports simulation of lightweight, complex-shaped floating structures in transient free-surface flows without explicit interface reconstruction or surface-normal evaluation.
method: Combine volume-based hydrodynamic loads with Newton–Euler rigid-body updates.
Iteratively feed back the mismatch between pressure-projected fictitious-fluid and rigid-body velocities within each time step.
Analyze when Passively Moving Solid projection and Newton–Euler updates produce identical rigid-body velocities.
evidence_signal: Iterative coupling remained stable across tested cube specific gravities of 0.1–1.0, while settling-disk and dam-break benchmarks agreed with published results and experimental trends.
watch_item: Strong coupling requires repeated updates per time step; all reported production runs met the residual tolerance, but computational overhead is not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Partitioned iterative FD-SPH for fluid-rigid-body interaction: Stability and validation for lightweight floating bodies
